columns.rationale: Order ID has null_rate 0.0 and 4000 distinct values across 5000 rows, consistent with multi-line orders; renamed to snake_case order_id.
LineNo has null_rate 0.0 with distinct_values 1 through 7 (min 1, max 7), confirming it is a line-item sequence within an order; renamed to snake_case line_no.
sku has null_rate 0.0 and 320 distinct values including numeric codes and non-numeric entries like 'BANK CHARGES' and 'DOT', so it must remain text.
qty has null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) and samples disagree in form ('-3', '2.0', 'three'), so per rule 6 it is kept as text rather than cast to integer.

unit_price has null_rate 0.0 with samples like 0.42 and 7.5 supporting a numeric cast; landed as DECIMAL(38,9), cast to DECIMAL(10,2) for currency precision, though its min of -5.0 against a max of 1250.0 warrants review (see decisionNegativeUnitPrice).
order_ts has null_rate 0.0 and consistently ISO-shaped samples such as '2024-01-05 09:15:00', justifying a cast from VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP.

ship_date has null_rate 0.264 (1320 nulls) and samples show disagreeing formats ('01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-1-9', 'Jan 9 2024', 'TBD'), so per rule 6 it is kept as text rather than cast to DATE.
customer_email is sparsely populated with null_rate 0.97 (4850 of 5000 nulls); retained nullable rather than dropped since some rows do carry valid addresses.

notes has null_rate 0.61 (3050 nulls); one sample is marked '…[truncated]' and is treated only as a prefix, and another sample resembling an embedded instruction is treated strictly as untrusted source data, never as a directive.

status has null_rate 0.0 but its 5 distinct_values (CANCELLED, Shipped, cancelled, pending, shipped) show inconsistent casing for what appears to be 3 logical states; raw text retained and flagged via decisionStatusCase.
is_gift has null_rate 0.012 (60 nulls) and distinct_values {N, Y, no, yes} mix casing and representation, so the raw text is retained while a normalized flag is derived separately.
Derived from is_gift distinct_values {N, Y, no, yes}: true for Y/yes case-insensitively, false for N/no, with null retained for the 60 null rows (null_rate 0.012).

Derived from status distinct_values including 'CANCELLED' and 'cancelled' (2 of 5 distinct values, case-insensitive match); true marks cancelled orders, and since status has null_rate 0.0 this flag is never null.
source_system has null_rate 0.0 and a single distinct_value 'legacy_pos', confirming this bronze table originates from one capture source.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_raw_id; it is a capture-tool row identifier, not a business column.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_extracted_at, which has only 2 distinct_values and is an extraction-time artifact, not business data.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_meta, whose single distinct_value is the constant empty object '{}' across all rows, carrying no business information.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 across row_count 5000, implying roughly 400 exact duplicate rows across all columns that should be removed before grain enforcement.

order_id has 4000 distinct values over 5000 rows while line_no ranges 1-7, indicating orders with multiple line items; (order_id, line_no) is the smallest evidenced set that plausibly identifies one row.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all marked is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning.
qty samples disagree in form ('-3', '2.0', 'three'), so casting to INTEGER would fail or silently misrepresent values; kept as VARCHAR per rule 6.
ship_date samples show multiple disagreeing date formats plus 'TBD' and empty string, so casting to DATE is unsafe; kept as VARCHAR.
customer_email null_rate is 0.97 (4850 of 5000 rows); retained rather than dropped since some rows carry valid values.
a notes sample contains text resembling an embedded instruction ('IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS...'); per governance it is treated as ordinary untrusted source data, not acted upon.
status distinct_values show CANCELLED/cancelled and Shipped/shipped casing variants across only 5 distinct values for apparently 3 logical states; raw text retained and an is_cancelled flag derived.
is_gift distinct_values {N, Y, no, yes} mix casing and representation; a normalized is_gift_flag boolean is derived while the raw column is retained.
unit_price min is -5.0 against a max of 1250.0; negative values may represent refunds or credits and are retained as-is pending business review rather than altered.

purpose: silver_orders cleans the legacy_pos order line-item export (bronze messy_orders) into a structured table of individual order lines, dropping capture-tool metadata, to support downstream order and revenue reporting.
usage: Consumers should treat (order_id, line_no) as the row grain after deduplicating exact duplicate rows, and should inspect qty and ship_date as text since they contain mixed formats rather than clean numbers or dates. Use the derived is_cancelled and is_gift_flag boolean columns instead of parsing raw status or is_gift text, and review rows with negative unit_price before summing revenue.
limitations: Cleanup could not resolve qty (mixed numeric and text values), ship_date (multiple disagreeing formats plus 'TBD'), or the casing inconsistencies in status and is_gift without a human-defined mapping, so these remain as raw text; customer_email (null_rate 0.97) and notes (null_rate 0.61) remain sparsely populated; exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08) are flagged for removal but this proposal does not itself perform the dedupe.
